00090| /// PR #965 review: "All CI/CD warnings, and errors must be also fixed.
00091| /// Including all false positives and false negatives."
00092| ///
00093| /// `actions/deploy-pages` accepts at most a 600 000 ms wait. On `main` run
00094| /// 31090830031 the artifact uploaded successfully (15.7 MB, id 8966823763) and
00095| /// the action then reported `Current status: deployment_queued` for that entire
00096| /// default before `Timeout reached, aborting!` — a red pipeline caused by
00097| /// GitHub's Pages deployment queue rather than by anything in the commit. The
00098| /// next push deployed green with no code change, which is the signature of a
00099| /// false positive. Pin the documented maximum rather than supplying the
00100| /// unsupported 1 200 000 ms value that the action silently clamps, and keep
00101| /// the job's own budget above it.
00102| #[test]
00103| fn pages_deploy_uses_the_actions_maximum_supported_wait() {
00104|     const DEPLOY_ACTION_MAXIMUM_MS: u64 = 600_000;
00105| 
00106|     let workflow = release_workflow();
00107|     let deploy_demo = job_block(&workflow, "deploy-pages");
00108| 
00109|     let timeout_ms = deploy_demo
00110|         .split("actions/deploy-pages@v5")
00111|         .nth(1)
00112|         .and_then(|after| after.split_once("timeout: "))
00113|         .and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split_whitespace().next())
00114|         .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u64>().ok())
00115|         .expect("the deploy-pages step should pin an explicit `timeout:` in milliseconds");
00116| 
00117|     assert!(
00118|         timeout_ms == DEPLOY_ACTION_MAXIMUM_MS,
00119|         "deploy-pages accepts at most {DEPLOY_ACTION_MAXIMUM_MS} ms, got {timeout_ms} ms"
00120|     );
00121| 
00122|     let job_budget_ms = job_block(&workflow, "deploy-pages")
00123|         .split_once("timeout-minutes: ")
00124|         .and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.split_whitespace().next())
00125|         .and_then(|value| value.parse::<u64>().ok())
00126|         .map(|minutes| minutes * 60_000)
00127|         .expect("deploy-pages should declare timeout-minutes");
00128| 
00129|     assert!(
00130|         job_budget_ms > timeout_ms,
00131|         "the deploy-pages job budget ({job_budget_ms} ms) must exceed the deployment wait \
00132|          ({timeout_ms} ms), or `timeout-minutes` kills the job before the wait can help"
00133|     );
00134| }

00193| #[test]
00194| fn wait_for_pages_deployment_is_marker_authoritative() {
00195|     // Issue #479 (root cause, take 2): the live-Pages freshness probe used to
00196|     // require the raw deploy SHA to appear in the served index BODY
00197|     // (`grep -Fq "$expected_sha" "$index_file"`). That coupled the probe to every
00198|     // root page embedding the commit SHA verbatim. When the issue #479 landing
00199|     // page shipped at `/` WITHOUT cache-busted asset refs, the stamped index
00200|     // never contained the SHA, so the probe ran the full 300s and timed out --
00201|     // failing the whole pipeline and (via the desktop-release gate) suppressing
00202|     // every desktop build. The probe is now marker-authoritative: GitHub Pages
00203|     // deploys atomically, so deployment.json advertising "sha":"<expected_sha>"
00204|     // is sufficient proof the matching stamped index is live.
00205|     let manifest_dir = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/..");
00206|     let wait_script = fs::read_to_string(format!(
00207|         "{manifest_dir}/scripts/wait-for-pages-deployment.sh"
00208|     ))
00209|     .unwrap();
00210| 
00211|     // The marker SHA is the authoritative freshness signal.
00212|     assert!(
00213|         wait_script.contains("${expected_sha}") && wait_script.contains("\"$marker_file\""),
00214|         "wait script should require the deployment.json marker to advertise the expected SHA"
00215|     );
00216|     // The brittle "index body must contain the SHA" requirement must be gone.
00217|     assert!(
00218|         !wait_script.contains("-Fq \"$expected_sha\" \"$index_file\""),
00219|         "issue #479 regression: the probe must NOT hard-require the raw SHA in the index body -- \
00220|          a valid root page without cache-busted asset refs would hang the probe for the full timeout"
00221|     );
00222|     // But the defensive placeholder guards (catch a half-run stamp step) remain.
00223|     assert!(
00224|         wait_script.contains("__FORMAL_AI_ASSET_VERSION__")
00225|             && wait_script.contains("__FORMAL_AI_VERSION__"),
00226|         "wait script should still reject an index that retains un-stamped placeholders"
00227|     );
00228| }

00298| #[test]
00299| fn test_job_skips_non_code_changes() {
00300|     // Issue #442: the `test` job ran whenever the `changelog` job was *skipped*.
00301|     // `changelog` is skipped precisely when there are no code changes (docs-only
00302|     // commits, .gitkeep edits, changelog-fragment-only commits), so the
00303|     // `needs.changelog.result == 'skipped'` clause turned "nothing relevant
00304|     // changed" into "run the entire test suite". This regression guard pins the
00305|     // corrected gating: `test` keys off the detect-changes outputs, exactly like
00306|     // `lint` and `coverage`, and never resurrects the changelog-skip escape.
00307|     let workflow = release_workflow();
00308|     let test = job_block(&workflow, "test");
00309| 
00310|     assert!(
00311|         !test.contains("needs.changelog.result == 'skipped'"),
00312|         "test job must not run merely because the changelog check was skipped; \
00313|          a skipped changelog means there were no code changes (issue #442)"
00314|     );
00315|     assert!(
00316|         !test.contains("needs.changelog.result == 'success'"),
00317|         "test job should be decoupled from the changelog check and gate on the \
00318|          change detector instead (issue #442)"
00319|     );
00320|     // Issue #1017 added `base`, which resolves the base-branch commit once so
00321|     // every gate merges the same one. Assert the dependency rather than the
00322|     // exact list, so adding a dependency cannot break a contract that is about
00323|     // `detect-changes`.
00324|     assert!(
00325|         test.contains("needs: [detect-changes")
00326|             && test.lines().any(|line| {
00327|                 line.trim().starts_with("needs:") && line.contains("detect-changes")
00328|             }),
00329|         "test job should depend on detect-changes so it can gate on its outputs"
00330|     );
00331|     assert!(
00332|         test.contains("needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'"),
00333|         "test job should run when code files changed"
00334|     );
00335|     assert!(
00336|         test.contains("needs.detect-changes.outputs.rs-changed == 'true'"),
00337|         "test job should run when Rust sources changed"
00338|     );
00339|     assert!(
00340|         test.contains("needs.detect-changes.outputs.toml-changed == 'true'"),
00341|         "test job should run when Cargo manifests changed"
00342|     );
00343|     // Issue #1107: `workflow-changed` is true for any file under
00344|     // `.github/workflows/`, so gating the compiled test matrix on it made an
00345|     // edit to a scheduled benchmark pay for the whole suite. What the matrix
00346|     // cares about is the pipeline it runs inside -- its own definition, a
00347|     // composite action it calls, or a script those run.
00348|     assert!(
00349|         test.contains("needs.detect-changes.outputs.pipeline-changed == 'true'"),
00350|         "test job should run when the pipeline it runs inside changed"
00351|     );
00352|     assert!(
00353|         !test.contains("github.event_name == 'push'")
00354|             && test.contains("github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'"),
00355|         "issue #846 requires pushes to obey detect-changes while manual \
00356|          dispatch remains unconditional"
00357|     );
00358|     assert!(
00359|         // Issue #808 / CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 10: `always()` also runs
00360|         // the job when the *run* is cancelled, which is not what this gate wants.
00361|         // `!cancelled()` is enough to stop a skipped `detect-changes` from
00362|         // cascading -- any status-check function disables the auto-skip.
00363|         test.contains("!cancelled()") && !test.contains("always()"),
00364|         "test job needs !cancelled() so the skipped detect-changes dependency \
00365|          does not cascade on workflow_dispatch"
00366|     );
00367| }

00433| /// Issue #812: run 29767811026 reported `Test (ubuntu-latest)` as failed with
00434| /// every test passing -- the suite finished 1.1 s before `timeout-minutes: 15`
00435| /// killed the job. The budget must exceed the measured cost, and the step must
00436| /// say so out loud before the margin is eaten again.
00437| #[test]
00438| fn test_job_budget_exceeds_the_measured_suite_cost_and_warns_before_it_is_eaten() {
00439|     let workflow = release_workflow();
00440|     let test_job = job_block(&workflow, "test");
00441| 
00442|     // Issue #1017: the cap has to clear the budget by more than the job's
00443|     // unbudgeted setup -- checkout, disk cleanup, the data-file and self-AST
00444|     // census gates and the doc tests measured 455s on run 31937348472 -- or the
00445|     // job clock still wins and the overrun is reported as `cancelled`.
00446|     //
00447|     // Issue #1081 replaced the two exact numbers this used to pin with floors,
00448|     // and both moved the same day. Pinning an exact budget is what makes a
00449|     // budget unable to grow when the work under it grows, which is how the
00450|     // macOS specification shard reached 100.1% of its budget twice with no
00451|     // warning; the arithmetic that decides what the numbers should be now
00452|     // lives in `tests/unit/ci-cd/job_budget_fit.rs`, which recomputes the whole
00453|     // job from the workflow instead of memorising one figure from it. What
00454|     // this test still defends is the shape: a plain-number cap, a budget on
00455|     // the suite, and the wrapper that makes the overrun red rather than grey.
00456|     let cap_minutes: u64 = test_job
00457|         .lines()
00458|         .find_map(|line| line.trim().strip_prefix("timeout-minutes:"))
00459|         .and_then(|value| value.trim().parse().ok())
00460|         .expect("the test job declares a plain-number timeout-minutes");
00461|     // PR #1188 (R1188-U9) runs the suite as five shards of prebuilt
00462|     // executables, a fifth of it about 450s (run 37802763478), so the floors
00463|     // are per shard: 15 minutes of shard work behind a 25-minute backstop.

00656| /// them -- so they are left as they are rather than "fixed" against a fault
00657| /// they do not have.

00689| /// `scripts/free-runner-disk.sh` to survive, and a job that exhausts `/` takes
00690| /// the runner down with no failed step and no log to download. A cached target
00691| /// tree measured 930 MB per job on top of that.

00694| /// `external-benchmarks.yml` cached it unnoticed. It now reads every workflow;
00695| /// this test pins that it does, because a policy enforced over part of the tree
00696| /// reports compliance it has not checked.

00701|         .expect("disk usage policy guard should be readable");
00702|

00704|         guard.contains(r#"fs::read_dir(".github/workflows")"#),
00705|         "the disk policy must sweep the workflow directory, or a workflow it \
00706|          does not list can cache the target tree unnoticed"
00707|     );
00708| 
00709|     let dir = format!("{manifest_dir}/.github/workflows");
00710|     let mut checked = 0;
00711|     for entry in fs::read_dir(&dir).expect("workflow directory should be readable") {
00712|         let path = entry.expect("directory entry").path();
00713|         if path.extension().is_none_or(|ext| ext != "yml") {
00714|             continue;
00715|         }
00716|         let workflow = fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("workflow should be readable");
00717|         assert!(
00718|             !workflow.lines().any(|line| line.trim() == "target"),
00719|             "{} caches the target tree, which issue #534 forbids",
00720|             path.display()

00722|         checked += 1;
